evals.prompt: We just finished a build sprint on ~/workspace/co-created/the target repository for a client. Before I hand it over I need it explained properly to three kinds of people: the marketing users, whoever picks up the code next, and their CTO who is not that technical. Can you set that up?
evals.expected_output: Scaffolds docs/explainer with the three audience documents grounded in code, ledgers per document, a kb/ and gates/ plan, measured (not quoted) gate numbers, and an honest built-vs-not-built section; states what is not gated yet.

evals.prompt: write me a repo primer for the agentbox management-api so an agent can actually answer questions about it from source, plus a short page for humans
evals.expected_output: Builds the AI half (passages within the scope boundary, ingest into a <repo>-kb namespace, question sets) and a human index following the seven questions; applies the index law after ingest.

evals.prompt: explain what this product does to my CEO in a page, she'll ask what it costs and what could go wrong
evals.expected_output: One for-executives document in board-memo register with the five trust properties, built/blocked/deferred table, costs only from documented sources, and a decisions checklist; no invented numbers.

evals.prompt: Build an explainer site for the target repository for an experienced engineer who did not write it and is wary of AI-generated filler. Explain the code as it stands, why it is shaped that way, and where to look. Don't narrate how the site was made.
evals.expected_output: Sections the site by the system's anatomy (repository, runtime, each service, each lane, consoles, tenant, operating it), not by evidence journeys; writes chapters as Markdown with front matter rendered by a dependency-free build into a reading shell with a source pane; every mechanism claim carries a src:path#Lx-Ly link the build validates; runs the research → write → independent check → revise pipeline; passes scripts/voice-lint.sh with hits=0 (no 'this guide', 'evidence', 'actual/real', drills, fixtures, fix history, media provenance), the target build, a range check and scripts/anatomy-coverage.mjs with no uncovered anchor; drafts on the connected node model in the background rather than through the Loom scaffold; keeps the ledger, receipts and completion audit out of the reader text; records the result in project-state.

evals.prompt: Start the executive explainer for ~/workspace/co-created/the target repository for a technically literate CEO or investor, following walkthroughs/executive/teaching-contract.md. Produce only this slice: chapters 1 (purpose and people) and 2 (one campaign change) as Markdown with front matter; one diagram of request to publication; two or three labelled screenshots of a headline change and preview; one 30 to 60 second captioned clip of chapter 2's journey with local narration; and run the gates on each. One src: range in the supplied fact sheet is outside its file. Work on the local model only; when a gate stays red after the capped attempts, write a hand-up packet and continue.
evals.expected_output: Two chapters in the executive register that pass voice-lint and the target build; the diagram, screenshots and clip produced through the specialist handoffs with receipts (pocket-tts narration, ComfyUI illustration labelled as illustration, ffmpeg receipt, captions); gates recorded per chapter; exactly one hand-up packet for the seeded bad range, written after a changed retry rather than an identical one, with the run continuing on unblocked work; no cloud model calls from the run; project facts kept in the engagement fixtures, not the skill.
expectations: Chapters 1 and 2 exist as Markdown with front matter, written in the executive register rather than an engineer's
Every src: link in the produced chapters resolves to a file and its line range is inside that file
scripts/voice-lint.sh reports 0 hits on every produced chapter
The out-of-range citation supplied in the fact sheet appears in no chapter
Exactly one hand-up packet was written for that out-of-range citation, after a retry that changed something, and the run continued on unblocked work
A request-to-publication diagram exists as both source and a render the reader can see
The screenshots were captured from the running application, with mode and input identity labelled, not authored as markup
A clip of 30 to 60 seconds exists with captions, a transcript, narration from the local speech service and a render receipt
Generated illustration is labelled as illustration and never presented as software behaviour
The media specialists were discovered through the catalogue and loaded, rather than their work improvised in shell
No provider other than the pinned local profile answered any request
Gate results are recorded per chapter in the production record, with the date and revision
Project facts stayed in the engagement fixtures and the skill tree was not modified by the run
